Not an official Festo app. A guide for sales conversations. Product details and part numbers may be incomplete or out of date. Always check on festo.com before quoting or ordering.
Automation for a world in motion.

Never sell just one part.
Show the whole solution.

Festo supplies individual parts that engineers combine into a system. In every conversation, offer the accessories or related products.

Core questions

Identify pneumatic & electric automation opportunities and future projects with these questions.

Process and applications

  • Could you walk me through your production process?
  • Where do you experience the most downtime or bottlenecks?

Pneumatics

  • What are the main pneumatic applications in your operation?
  • Are there any recurring issues with your pneumatic systems?

Electric automation

  • Where are you currently using electric drives or motion control, who is your current supplier and what protocol is it?
  • Are there any applications you're considering moving from pneumatic to electric?

Maintenance and reliability

  • What causes most of your unplanned downtime?
  • What would make maintenance easier for your team?

Energy and sustainability

  • Is reducing energy consumption a priority for your site?

Projects and future plans

  • What new projects or upgrades are planned over the next 6-12 months?
  • If you could improve one thing in your production process, what would it be?

End-of-visit questions

  • What would be most valuable for us to help you with?
  • Who else is involved in automation decisions?
  • What would be the best next step from your perspective?

Simple follow-up questions

Use these after any interesting answer

  • Can you tell me more about that?
  • Why is that important?
  • What's the impact on production?
  • How are you handling that today?

Push-in fittings

Push the tube in and it holds. Press the release ring to take it out.

Every fitting on the Festo metric push-in fittings poster, by shape. Tap one for its sizes and part numbers.

Fittings with a thread

Screw into a port; the tube pushes in.

Distributors

One thread in, several tubes out.

Tube to tube connectors

Join, split or reduce tubes, or blank one off.

Mini series QSM

For 2 to 6 mm tube and M3 to M8 threads.

NPQH metal fittings

Brass, chemically nickel-plated.

Flow control and check valves

Set cylinder speed, or hold it in position.

Sizes and threads
Tube OD
4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 mm; mini series 2, 3, 4, 6 mm; QS-G3/4 to 22 mm
Metric thread
M3, M5, M6, M7, M8
R thread
R1/8, R1/4, R3/8, R1/2 (taper, sealing coating)
G thread
G1/8, G1/4, G3/8, G1/2, G3/4
Pressure

Temperature

Media
Compressed air, vacuum, water (max. 6 bar at 50 °C)
Tube size, not bore sizeFittings are chosen by the tube outside diameter, then the thread in the port. Ask for both.
Ask the customer
  1. Tube outside diameter
  2. Thread in the port (metric, R or G, and size)
  3. Shape: straight, elbow, tee, Y, distributor
  4. How many: packs of 1, 10, 20, 50 or 100 depending on the part
  5. Any special conditions: heat, food, chemicals, welding

Fittings for special jobs

When standard QS is not enough. Each is paired with the tubing it is tested with.

High temperature and pressure
NPQH + PFAN0–150 °C16 barUp to 150 °C. Food-safe, FDA-listed material, resists cleaning agents.
NPQH + PAN-R0–80 °C20 barPressure up to 2 MPa, for example after a DPA pressure booster.
NPQM + PAN-MF−20–70 °C16 barMeets DIN 73378. For mobile pneumatics.
NPQR + PUN-H-SF−20–80 °C13 barResists kinking and hydrolysis. Good for water and humid areas.
Food, chemicals and washdown
NPQR + PUN-H-F−20–60 °C10 barFood-safe to EC 1935/2004, FDA-listed materials. Hydrolysis-resistant, fine with water.
NPQP + PLN−20–60 °C10 barEconomical plastic fitting listed for the food zone. Resists cleaning agents.

CRQS + PTFEN−15–120 °C10 barStainless steel push-in, CRC 4. For aggressive acids and alkalis. EC 1935/2004.
Special environments
NPQH + PUN-V0-C0–60 °C10 barWelding spatter. Tubing wall 2 mm on every size.
QS-V0 + PAN-V00–60 °C10 barRight next to welding spatter, with double-walled tubing.
NPQM + PUN-V0−20–60 °C10 barFlame-retardant, tubing tested to DIN 5510-2.
NPQM + PUN-CM−20–60 °C10 barAntistatic tubing with a solid metal fitting. Protects electronics.
NPQE-F1A + PUN-H−5–60 °C8 barFor Li-ion battery production. No metals with over 1% copper, zinc or nickel.
NPQO + PUN-H-F…-NT0–60 °C10 barOxygen and breathing gas in medical devices. ISO 15001 and ISO 18562.

Temperatures and pressures are for the tubing and fitting combination. Check chemicals in Media resistance.

Cylinders

Compressed air in, straight-line push and pull out.

ADN, DSNU and DSBC cover most enquiries. Each is built to an ISO standard, so it swaps for other brands of the same standard. DPDM is the short multi-mount compact cylinder, DFM adds a built-in guide for torque and side loads, and CRDNG and CRDSNU are stainless steel for harsh environments and the food sector.

Cylinder types – tap one for details

DPDM – Compact Cylinder, Multi-mount

Short compact cylinder with a wide range of mounting interfaces.

DPDMDPDM-Q protection against rotationInterchangeable with DMM
  • Double-acting, and single-acting pushing (S) or pulling (P)
  • With or without protection against rotation (DPDM-Q)
  • All mounting interfaces compatible with compact cylinder DMM, but noticeably shorter and lighter
  • Mounts at the front or rear, vertically or horizontally
  • Variants:
    • T through piston rod, H through hollow piston rod (can carry vacuum or compressed air)
    • T1 heat-resistant seals, 0 to +120 °C (from Ø 10)
    • F1A for lithium-ion battery production
  • Typical use: stopping small parts
Piston Ø
6–32 mm
Stroke
Ø 6–10: 5–30 mm
Ø 16–32: 5–50 mm
Single-acting: 5, 10, 15 mm
Operating pressure
Up to 8 bar
Temperature
−10 to +80 °C
T1: 0 to +120 °C
Port
M5 (Ø 6–25), G1/8 (Ø 32)
Cushioning
Elastic cushioning rings/plates at both ends
Common accessories

  • Ø 25/32: T-slot proximity switch SMT-8M PNP, M8 3-pin, 0.3 m: 574334
  • One-way flow control valve GRLA or VFOH, for example GRLA-M5-QS-4-D: 193138, and push-in fittings QS
  • Rod clevis SG, rod eye SGS, self-aligning rod coupler FK, suction cup adapter AD

Source: Festo "Compact cylinder DPDM, multi-mount", 2026/07.

DFM – Guided Drive Double Acting

Drive and guide in a single housing.

DFMDFM-B function-optimisedGF plain bearingKF ball bearing
  • Minimal space requirement and mounting time
  • High resistance to torsion, torques and lateral forces
  • GF plain-bearing guide: high rigidity, large-diameter guide rods and four plain-bearing bushes
  • KF recirculating ball bearing guide: for movements involving torque loads
  • DFM-B variants:
    • Strokes up to 400 mm
    • Precision end-position adjustment, advancing (AJ) and retracting (EJ)
    • Pneumatic cushioning, adjustable (PPV)
    • Shock absorber, self-adjusting, progressive (YSRW)
  • Typical uses: clamping, lifting, pushing and stopping, for example in conveyor technology
Piston Ø
DFM 6–100 mm
DFM-B 12–63 mm
Stroke
DFM 5–200 mm
DFM-B 10–400 mm
Cushioning
Elastic cushioning rings/plates (P). DFM-B also PPV or YSRW
Mounting
From the top, underneath, sideways or at the front. Through-hole or female thread
Port
M3 (Ø 6–10) up to G3/8 (Ø 80–100)
Sensing
Via proximity switch in the profile slot
Common accessories
  • Proximity switch PNP, T-slot, M8 3-pin, 0.3 m (Ø 12–100): 574334
  • Ø 6 and 10: C-slot switch SMT-10G PNP, M8 3-pin, 0.3 m: 547863
  • Slot cover ABP-5-S, 2x 0.5 m: 151680
  • One-way flow control valve GRLA and push-in fittings
  • Centring sleeves ZBH, 4 or 6 included

Source: Festo "Guided drives DFM/DFM-B", 2026/05. DFM-B Ø 12 uses C-slot switches (SMT-10M or SME-10M).

CRDNG – ISO 15552 Stainless Steel Double Acting

Stainless-steel cylinder for harsh environments and the food sector.

CRDNGCRDNGS swivel flangeISO 15552
  • Based on ISO 15552
  • High-alloy stainless steel, corrosion resistance class 4 (very high corrosion stress)
  • NSF-H1 compliant grease and wipers to BGVV guidelines, so it can be used in the food sector
  • Pneumatic cushioning adjustable at both ends (PPV) and position sensing as standard
  • Variants:
    • CRDNGS with swivel flange
    • S2 through piston rod
    • S6 heat-resistant seals, 0 to +120 °C (not for direct contact with food)
  • Matching stainless-steel mountings and accessories

CRDSNU – ISO 6432 Stainless Steel Double Acting

Stainless-steel round cylinder in an easy-to-clean design.

CRDSNUCRDSNU-BISO 6432 (Ø 12–25)

Ask the customer
  1. Bore and stroke (or the old part number)
  2. Single or double acting
  3. Male or female rod thread
  4. Cushioning: rubber bumpers, adjustable or self-adjusting
  5. Do they need position sensors?
  6. How is it mounted at each end?
Goes with
  • Mountings: foot, flange, clevis, trunnion, rod eye and rod clevis
  • Sensors: proximity switches in the cylinder slot
  • Flow control to set the speed, and push-in fittings with tubing
  • Valve to drive it, fed from air preparation

Questions to ask

Say it out loud.

1

What's the stroke and bore, and is it replacing an existing cylinder?

2

How is it mounted, and what's on the rod end?

3

Do you need position sensing, and are you using proximity sensors?

4

How is it being controlled? Do you have a valve or valve terminal already?

5

Does the cylinder need speed control adjustment?

6

Is the load side-loaded or does it need guiding?

Use the questions to uncover opportunities for further discussion.

Fast-switching valves · MH
Use whenVery short switching times and high cycle rates are needed
Exact, repeatable timing matters, for example dispensing or gluing
Suitable areas of application
  • Sorting parts using an air ejector
  • Flap control systems
  • Gluing and dispensing
  • Packaging
  • Pick & place vacuum applications (continuous holding not possible)
Key features
  • Repetition accuracy ≤ 0.2 ms
  • Over 500 million cycles, even in 24-hour continuous operation
  • Available with or without built-in fast-switching electronics
  • Direct activation from a standard PLC with 24 V DC

  • Pilot valves for single- and double-acting quarter-turn and linear actuators with NAMUR interface to VDI/VDE 3845, such as DAPS, DFPB and DLP

  • Cost-optimised version (plastic cover, brass armature, IP65 coils) or application-optimised version (aluminium cover, stainless-steel armature, IP65 and Ex coils)
  • For Zone 1 (Ex-ia, Ex-mb), Zone 2 (Ex-nA) and Class I Div 1

Key features
  • Generously sized profiles for maximum rigidity and load capacity. Its high performance often allows a smaller size
  • Motor position freely selectable on 4 sides, and can be changed at any time
  • Toothed belt in chloroprene rubber, or coated PU with steel cords for resistance to certain cooling lubricants
  • Options: protected guide, central lubrication, displacement encoder, clamping unit, extended or additional slide
  • EX3 version for potentially explosive areas
Complete systemMatched motors EMMT-AS (servo), EMMB-ST or EMMT-ST (stepper), servo drives CMMT-AS or CMMT-ST, and an axial kit EAMM.

6050 … 1,0001.111,550±0.01

Maximum values per size. They are not reached at the same time, so size the axis in Electric Motion Sizing before quoting.

Key features
  • NSF-H1 lubricant for the food zone. Suitable for Li-ion battery production
  • Stainless-steel cover strip: clean surface, fewer particles for cleanrooms, less dirt ingress in harsh conditions
  • Wide design ELGD-BS-WD: lower profile and 30% lighter, for handling systems that do not need such high feed forces
  • Several screw pitches, so the smallest motor can be chosen for the speed and force needed
  • Options: extended or additional slide, sealing air connection, guide axis ELFD without drive
Good to knowMax. acceleration 15 m/s². Reversing backlash 0.15 mm. Speed and force figures depend on screw pitch and stroke.

  • Servo and stepper motors with their controllers, for example EMMT and CMMT
  • Handling systems: gantries and pick-and-place built from axes
Ask the customer
  1. Load and stroke
  2. How many positions, and how accurate?
  3. Speed or cycle time
  4. How is it controlled: I/O, IO-Link or fieldbus?
  5. Would a pneumatic cylinder be enough? Compare in CO2 and TCO guide

General overview to help the conversation. Check the data sheet or the online shop before quoting a part number.

Pneumatic vs electric

Both have a place. Know when to offer each.

Pneumatic

Benefits

  • Simple and robust
  • Low cost to buy
  • Fast, simple end-to-end movement
  • Easy to install and maintain
  • Copes well with harsh, dirty or wet areas

Limitations

  • Best suited to set end positions
  • Compressed air costs energy, and leaks waste it
  • Less control of speed and force along the stroke
  • Needs an air supply and air preparation

Electric

Benefits

  • Precise positioning to many points
  • Speed, force and position are programmable
  • Uses energy mainly when moving
  • Quiet and clean
  • Feedback and diagnostics

Limitations

  • Higher initial cost
  • More set-up: motor, controller, cabling and software
  • Needs more know-how to commission
  • Can be more than a simple job needs

Ask which jobs only need end positions, and which need precise control.

Basics

The know-how behind the product pages. Start here if pneumatics is new to you.

Read the label

Most enquiries are "another one of these". The label tells you what it is.

Part number and type codeThe part number is the 6 to 8 digit number on the label. Quote it to order exactly the same item. The type code describes the product: read it left to right.
Cylinder
DSBC-32-100-PPVA-N3
  • DSBCRange: ISO standard cylinder
  • 32Bore: piston diameter in mm. Bigger bore, more force
  • 100Stroke: how far the rod moves, in mm
  • PPVAOptions: cushioning and a magnet for sensors
  • N3Version. Copy it exactly
Push-in fitting
QS-G1/4-8
  • QSRange: push-in fitting (QSL is the elbow version)
  • G1/4Thread that screws into the product
  • 8Tube size it takes: 8 mm outside diameter
Tubing
PUN-H-8X1,25-BL
  • PUN-HRange: polyurethane tubing
  • 8X1,258 mm outside diameter, 1.25 mm wall
  • BLColour: blue
Cylinder sensor
SMT-8M-A-PS-24V-E-2,5-OE
  • SMT-8MRange: electronic sensor that fits the cylinder slot
  • PSPNP output. NS means NPN
  • 24VSupply voltage
  • 2,5Cable length in metres
  • OEOpen cable end. M8 or M12 means a plug
  • A, EOther options. Copy them exactly

Codes vary by range. If in doubt, type the full part number or type code into festo.com.

Jargon buster

The words customers use, in plain English.

Cylinders
Bore
Inside diameter of the cylinder (the piston size). Sets the force.
Stroke
How far the rod travels, in mm.
Single-acting
Air pushes one way, a spring brings it back.
Double-acting
Air pushes both ways. The most common type.
Cushioning
Slows the piston at the end of travel so it doesn't bang.
ISO 15552
A standard size, so cylinders from different makers swap over.
Piston rod
The bar that moves in and out and does the work.
Rod eye / clevis
Fitting for the piston rod to connect the cylinder to something.
WH
Distance from the end of the cylinder to the start of the piston rod thread.
Magnetic piston
A magnet inside the piston so a sensor can detect it. Needed for proximity sensors.
Side load
A sideways force on the rod. Too much wears the cylinder out.
Guided cylinder
Extra guide rods stop twisting and take side load (DFM).
Rodless / linear drive
A carriage runs along the body, with no rod sticking out (DGC).
Mounting
How the cylinder is fixed, for example foot, flange, trunnion or clevis.
Valves
Solenoid valve
An electrically switched valve that directs the air.
Valve terminal
Several valves on one base with one electrical connection.
3/2
3 ports, 2 positions. Turns air on and off, or drives a single-acting cylinder.
5/2
5 ports, 2 positions. Drives a double-acting cylinder out and back.
5/3
5 ports, 3 positions. The middle position can stop or hold the cylinder.
Port numbers
1 is the supply, 2 and 4 go to the cylinder, 3 and 5 are exhausts.
Monostable / bistable
Monostable springs back when the signal stops (single solenoid). Bistable stays where it was last switched (double solenoid).
NC / NO
Normally closed or normally open: what the valve does with no signal.
Coil voltage
The voltage that switches the valve. 24 V DC is the most common.
Manual override
A button to switch the valve by hand when testing.
Pilot-operated
A small air signal helps switch the valve, so the coil can be small.
Flow rate (l/min)
How much air the valve passes. Too low makes the cylinder slow.
Manifold / sub-base
A block that several valves bolt onto to share the air supply.
Mechanically operated
Switched by a lever, roller or button instead of electricity.
Air and connections
bar
Unit of pressure. Factory air is typically around 6 bar.
Air preparation (FRL)
Filter, regulator, lubricator. Cleans the air and sets the pressure.
Micron (µm)
Filter rating. The smaller the number, the finer the filter.
Port
Where the air connects on a product.
G thread
Parallel pipe thread, written G1/8, G1/4 and so on. The usual thread in the UK.
M5
Small metric thread used on small valves and cylinders.
R / NPT thread
Tapered threads. Don't mix them with G threads.
Push-in fitting
Push the tube in to connect, press the collar to release.
Tube OD
Outside diameter of the tube. Must match the fitting.
Tube ID
Internal diameter of the tube. Applicable with old style fittings where the tube fits over a barbed fitting.
Flow control
Restricts the air to set how fast the cylinder moves.
Silencer
Quietens the air as it exhausts.
Air quality (ISO 8573-1)
The standard grading for how clean and dry the air is.
Dew point / dryer
The temperature at which water drops out of the air. A dryer removes that water.
Condensate drain
Lets collected water out of a filter, either by hand or automatically.
Lubricated vs oil-free
Most modern parts run on dry air. Once a system has been oiled, it must stay oiled.
Soft-start valve
Builds pressure slowly at switch-on so the machine doesn't jump.
Shut-off / lockout valve
Cuts off and vents the air for safe maintenance.
Non-return valve
Lets air flow one way only.
Leaks
Escaping air, which costs money in compressor electricity.
Sensors and electrics
Proximity sensor
Clips into the cylinder slot and detects the magnet on the piston.
PNP / NPN
Type of output signal. Must match the controller. PNP is the most common in the UK and Europe.
M8 / M12
Standard round plug sizes for sensors and cables.
PLC
The controller that runs the machine.
Fieldbus
A network linking devices to the PLC, for example PROFINET or EtherNet/IP.
IO-Link
A smart connection that sends settings and diagnostics as well as the signal.
Reed vs electronic sensor
SME is reed and SMT is electronic, with a longer life.
Analogue output
A variable signal (4–20 mA or 0–10 V) rather than just on/off.
IP rating
Protection against dust and water. IP65 and IP67 are common.
2-wire / 3-wire
How the sensor is wired. It must match the machine.
Electric drives
Axis
One direction of movement.
Handling system
Multiple direction of movement. Defined by X axis (forward & back) / Y axis (left & right) / Z axis (up & down)
Spindle vs toothed belt
A spindle is precise and strong. A belt is fast and covers long distances.
Servo / stepper motor
A servo is fast and accurate, using feedback. A stepper is simpler and cheaper.
Motor controller
The unit that powers and controls the motor.
Encoder
Tells the controller where the motor is.
Repeatability
How precisely the drive returns to the same spot.
Homing
Finding the start point after power-up.
Process and vacuum
Quarter-turn actuator
Turns a process valve 90° open or closed.
NAMUR
A standard mounting pattern, so a valve bolts straight onto an actuator.
Positioner
Sets a process valve to any position, not just open or closed.
Media
The liquid or gas flowing through a process valve.
Vacuum generator
Makes vacuum from compressed air.
ATEX
Rules for equipment in explosive atmospheres. Always pass to technical support.
Spring-return actuator / fail-safe
A spring moves the valve to a safe position if the air fails.
Ball / butterfly valve
The common types of process valve.
Sensor box
Shows whether the actuator is open or closed.
Suction cup
The rubber cup that holds the part.
Vacuum level (-kPa / %)
How strong the suction is.
Air-saving function
The ejector switches off once the vacuum is holding.
Blow-off pulse
A puff of air that releases the part.
Ordering and service
Configurable product
Built to order from a set of options, so check the lead time.
Core range - Blue Star
Festo's fast-delivery range, marked with a blue star on festo.com.
Wear parts / repair kit
Seals and similar parts for refurbishing instead of replacing.
Successor product
The replacement for a discontinued part.
UKCA / CE
The conformity marks for the UK and EU markets.

No term matches. Try a shorter word.

When to hand over

You don't need to know everything. Know when to ask.

Pass to technical support when
  • 1The customer wants you to size or calculate something: force, speed or air use.
  • 2Safety is involved: emergency stops, guarding, or holding a load if the air fails.
  • 3It's a hazardous area (ATEX), food, pharma or cleanroom application.
  • 4The load is heavy or moves vertically.
  • 5You can't find a direct replacement for an old part.
  • 6The customer is thinking of moving from pneumatic to electric.
  • 7You would be guessing.

Pneumatic FAQs

Common questions about pneumatics and Festo. Tap a question to see the answer.

About pneumatics
1What exactly is pneumatic automation, and how does it work?Show

Pneumatic automation involves using compressed air to drive machinery and control various processes. It works by converting the energy stored in compressed air into mechanical motion through actuators, often pneumatic cylinders, which then perform tasks like lifting, shifting, and pressing.

2What are the key advantages and limitations of using pneumatic automation compared to other technologies?Show

Advantages:

Safety: Pneumatic systems are inherently safe because they use air, which is non-flammable and less hazardous compared to electrical or hydraulic systems.

Simplicity and Reliability: These systems are relatively simple to design and maintain, leading to high reliability.

Speed and Efficiency: Pneumatic systems can operate at high speeds, making them efficient for numerous tasks.

Limitations:

Limited Force: The force output is generally less than that of hydraulic systems, limiting their use in heavy-duty applications.

Air Quality Sensitivity: Pneumatic systems require clean, dry air to prevent wear and tear, necessitating additional components for air treatment.

Energy Efficiency: Compressing air is energetically costly, making pneumatic systems less energy-efficient compared to electric systems in some cases.

3In which industries and applications is pneumatic automation commonly found?Show

Pneumatic automation is commonly found in industries like manufacturing, automotive, packaging, and pharmaceuticals. Applications include material handling, assembly operations, and packaging machinery.

4What are the main types of pneumatic cylinders, and how do they differ in function and use?Show

Single-Acting Cylinders: Use air pressure to move in one direction and a spring to return to the original position.

Double-Acting Cylinders: Use air pressure for movement in both directions, allowing for greater control and force application.

5What are the different ways to control pneumatic valves, and what are their typical applications?Show

Valve control can be manual, mechanical, pneumatic, or electronic, with applications ranging from simple on/off control to complex speed and sequence control in automated systems.

6Why are air filters, regulators, and lubricators (FRLs) crucial components in a pneumatic system, and how do they work?Show

Air Filters: Remove contaminants from the air, protecting the system from damage and wear.

Regulators: Control the air pressure to ensure consistent operation.

Lubricators: Add a lubricant to the air to reduce friction within pneumatic components.

7Besides cylinders and valves, what other essential components might be included in a pneumatic automation system?Show

Besides cylinders and valves, essential components may include connectors, tubes, pressure switches, and sensors for monitoring and controlling the system.

8How can I design a basic pneumatic system to achieve a specific task?Show

Designing a basic pneumatic system involves defining the task, selecting appropriate components (cylinders, valves, FRLs), and ensuring proper air supply and control logic to achieve the desired motion or process control.

9What are the most important safety considerations when designing and using pneumatic systems?Show

Important safety considerations include using pressure relief valves, ensuring components are rated for the maximum system pressure, and providing adequate guards and safety interlocks.

10How can I troubleshoot common problems like leaks, slow movement, or component failure in a pneumatic system?Show

Common problems can often be addressed by checking for leaks, ensuring proper lubrication, and verifying that all components are functioning correctly. Recommended maintenance practices include regular inspections, cleaning air filters, and replacing worn parts.

11What are the recommended maintenance practices to ensure the smooth operation and longevity of a pneumatic system?Show

Common problems can often be addressed by checking for leaks, ensuring proper lubrication, and verifying that all components are functioning correctly. Recommended maintenance practices include regular inspections, cleaning air filters, and replacing worn parts.

12What are intelligent pneumatic systems, and what unique benefits do they offer?Show

Intelligent pneumatic systems integrate sensors and control systems to optimize efficiency, adapt to changing conditions, and provide predictive maintenance capabilities, offering significant benefits over traditional systems.

13How can pneumatic automation systems be designed and operated with environmental considerations in mind?Show

Designing pneumatic systems with environmental considerations involves selecting energy-efficient components, ensuring optimal system pressure to minimize energy use, and using environmentally friendly lubricants.

14What are some exciting future trends in pneumatic automation, and how will they impact its use?Show

Exciting future trends in pneumatic automation include the integration of IoT technologies for smarter control, the development of more energy-efficient systems, and the application of advanced materials to reduce weight and improve performance, potentially expanding the use and efficiency of pneumatic systems in various industries.

15What is controlled pneumatics?Show

Controlled pneumatics refers to the precision control of pneumatic systems, where the movement, force, speed, and position of pneumatic actuators (such as cylinders) are regulated with high accuracy. This is achieved through advanced control systems and components like proportional valves, sensors, and electronic controllers that can modulate the flow and pressure of compressed air according to the requirements of a specific task or process.

21Does Festo offer pneumatic grippers for handling applications?Show

Yes, Festo offers a wide range of grippers for pneumatic solutions, catering to various industrial automation tasks, including pick-and-place operations, assembly processes, and handling tasks. Their gripper portfolio is designed to meet diverse application requirements, such as gripping force, size, and material compatibility, ensuring that there is a suitable solution for almost any task involving automated picking, holding, or moving of objects.

Among the types of pneumatic grippers Festo provides are:

Parallel Grippers: These grippers have jaws that move in parallel to each other to grip an object. They are versatile and can handle a wide range of part sizes and shapes. Parallel grippers are commonly used in applications where precision and reliability are critical.

Angular Grippers: Angular grippers have jaws that pivot, allowing them to grip parts from the side. This type of gripper is often used in tight spaces where a straight-on approach is not possible.

Bellows Grippers: These are used for delicate or irregular-shaped objects. The bellows expand to grip the object gently, making them ideal for handling fragile items.

Adaptive Grippers: These grippers can adjust their gripping force and shape to handle a wide variety of object sizes, shapes, and weights, making them highly versatile for applications with varying requirements.

Festo's grippers are known for their durability, precision, and efficiency, enhancing productivity in automated systems. They also offer customization options to fit specific application needs, such as grippers with sensors for position feedback or those made from materials compatible with specific environmental conditions (e.g., food-grade materials for processing and packaging applications). 27How does Festo contribute to sustainability?Show

Festo is deeply committed to sustainable automation, focusing on developing pneumatic automation products and solutions that contribute to energy efficiency, resource conservation, and environmental protection. Their approach to sustainability in pneumatic automation encompasses several key areas:

Energy-Efficient Products

Festo designs products that require less energy to operate without compromising performance. This includes energy-efficient pneumatic cylinders, valves, and drives that consume less compressed air, reducing the overall energy demand of the system. For instance, their latest developments often incorporate features that allow for lower operating pressures or optimized flow rates, thereby minimizing energy usage.

Smart and Connected Solutions

The integration of IoT (Internet of Things) technologies into Festo's pneumatic products enables smarter automation systems. These intelligent solutions can monitor and adjust their operation in real-time to optimize energy use, predict maintenance needs, and reduce waste. For example, smart sensors and predictive analytics can identify when a system is using more energy than necessary and adjust parameters automatically to improve efficiency.

Use of Recycled and Sustainable Materials

Festo is increasingly using recycled and environmentally friendly materials in their product manufacturing processes. This not only reduces the environmental impact of their products but also promotes a circular economy by making it easier to recycle components at the end of their lifecycle.

Training and Education

Understanding that knowledge is key to sustainability, Festo offers training and educational programs on energy efficiency and sustainable practices in automation. By educating engineers, technicians, and industry professionals, Festo helps spread sustainable practices throughout the industry.

Reducing Environmental Footprint

Beyond product design, Festo focuses on reducing the environmental footprint of its manufacturing operations. This includes efforts to decrease CO2 emissions, conserve water, and reduce waste. By leading by example, Festo aims to show how sustainable practices can be integrated into all aspects of business operations.

Sustainable Automation Solutions

Festo's solutions often target specific applications with potential for significant environmental impact improvements, such as water treatment, renewable energy sectors, and processes that benefit from reduced material use and waste. Their pneumatic systems are designed to be both energy-efficient and durable, ensuring long-term reliability and reduced need for replacements, thereby contributing to waste minimization.

In summary, Festo's commitment to sustainable automation with their pneumatic products is evident in their energy-efficient designs, adoption of smart technologies, use of sustainable materials, educational initiatives, and efforts to minimize their environmental footprint. These efforts not only benefit the environment but also provide economic advantages to users through reduced operational costs and enhanced system performance. For the latest initiatives and product offerings from Festo in sustainable automation, consulting their official website or contacting their representatives would provide the most current information.

28What specific products does Festo offer?Show

Festo offers a wide range of specific products across various categories in pneumatic automation. Here's a breakdown of some of their key product offerings:

Pneumatic Actuators:

Festo provides a diverse range of pneumatic actuators, including:

Pneumatic cylinders: Standard cylinders, compact cylinders, rodless cylinders, guided cylinders, and specialized cylinders for specific applications.

Rotary actuators: Rotary vane actuators, rack-and-pinion actuators, swivel modules, and rotary indexing tables.

Pneumatic Valves:

Festo offers a comprehensive selection of pneumatic valves for controlling the flow of compressed air, including:

Directional control valves: Solenoid valves, manually operated valves, mechanically operated valves, and air-piloted valves.

Proportional valves: Proportional directional control valves and proportional pressure control valves.

Safety valves: Pressure relief valves and emergency shutdown valves.

Process valves: Ball valves, butterfly valves, gate valves, and diaphragm valves.

Pneumatic Fittings and Tubing:

Festo provides a wide array of pneumatic fittings, tubing, and connectors, including:

Push-in fittings: One-touch fittings, quick connectors, threaded fittings, and tube-to-tube fittings.

Tubing: Polyurethane tubing, nylon tubing, fluoropolymer tubing, and various accessories such as tubing cutters and tube clamps.

Pneumatic Control Systems:

Festo offers pneumatic control systems and components for automation and process control, such as:

Valve terminals: Modular valve terminals, multipin valve terminals, and compact valve terminals.

Pneumatic controllers: Programmable logic controllers (PLCs), fieldbus systems (PROFIBUS, PROFINET, EtherCAT), and pneumatic positioning systems.

Pneumatic Grippers and Handling Systems:

Festo provides a range of pneumatic grippers and handling systems for robotic automation and material handling applications, including:

Parallel grippers, angular grippers, three-finger grippers, and special-purpose grippers.

Linear gantry systems, rotary indexing tables, pick-and-place units, and vacuum gripping systems.

Pneumatic Process Automation:

Festo offers pneumatic components and systems tailored for process automation applications, such as:

Control valves: Globe valves, angle valves, and diaphragm valves for precise control of process fluids.

Positioners: Pneumatic and electro-pneumatic positioners for accurate valve positioning and control.

Pneumatic Sensors and Accessories:

Festo provides a range of sensors and accessories to complement their pneumatic products, including:

Position sensors: Cylinder position sensors, proximity sensors, and magnetic field sensors.

Accessories: Air preparation units (filters, regulators, lubricators), shock absorbers, flow control valves, and pressure switches.
